questions.q: What must the Israelites do at the end of every seven years?
questions.a: At the end of every seven years the Israelites must cancel all debts.

questions.q: Why are debts to be canceled every seven years?
questions.a: Everyone will cancel that which he has loaned to a fellow Israelite because Yahweh has declared the cancelation of debts every seven years.

questions.q: From whom can Israelites continue to collect payment at the end of every seven years?
questions.a: The Israelites can continue to collect payment of a debt from a foreigner.

questions.q: Why should there be no poor among the Israelites?
questions.a: If they do all that Yahweh has commanded them, there should no longer be poor among them since Yahweh will bless them.

questions.q: What will happen to demonstrate that Yahweh has blessed Israel as he promised?
questions.a: Israel will lend to many nations, but will not borrow; Israel will rule over many nations, but the other nations will not rule over them.

questions.q: What are the Israelites told not to do if there is a poor man among them?
questions.a: The Israelites are told not to be selfish and refuse to help them.

questions.q: What should the Israelites be careful not to do when the seventh year, the year of remission is near?
questions.a: They should not refuse to give help to a poor man because the year of canceling debts is near.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do for the Israelites in return for giving generously to the poor?
questions.a: Yahweh will bless the Israelites in everything they do.

questions.q: Why is Israel commanded to give generously to their fellow Israelites, to the needy and the poor in their land?
questions.a: They should give generously because there will always be poor living among them.

questions.q: What are Israelites instructed to give a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman who is released to go free in the seventh year?
questions.a: They must provide for that person freely out of their flocks and their crops with which Yahweh their God has blessed them.

questions.q: What are the Israelites to remember as they give to the one they set free?
questions.a: The Israelites are told to remember that they were slaves in the land of Egypt and Yahweh freed them.

questions.q: What is an Israelite to do to a male or female slave who says that they do not want to leave?
questions.a: The Israelite is to pierce the slave’s ear, and he or she will be their slave forever.

questions.q: Why should it not seem difficult for the Israelite to let the slave go free?
questions.a: It should not be difficult because he has served them for six years and given them twice the value of a hired person.

questions.q: What must the people of Israel do with the firstborn males in their herd and their flock?
questions.a: They must set them aside for Yahweh and not use them for work or shear them.

questions.q: What are the Israelites to do with the firstborn animal if it is lame or blind or has any other defect?
questions.a: They must not sacrifice it to Yahweh, but instead they can eat it.

commentary.text: Verses 1–11 This year of release typified the grace of the gospel, in which is proclaimed the acceptable year of the Lord; and by which we obtain the release of our debts, that is, the pardon of our sins. The law is spiritual, and lays restraints upon the thoughts of the heart. We mistake, if we think thoughts are free from God's knowledge and check. That is a wicked heart indeed, which raises evil thoughts from the good law of God, as theirs did, who, because God had obliged them to the charity of forgiving, denied the charity of giving. Those who would keep from the act of sin, must keep out of their minds the very thought of sin. It is a dreadful thing to have the cry of the poor justly against us. Grudge not a kindness to thy brother; distrust not the providence of God. What thou doest, do freely, for God loves a cheerful giver, 2Co 9:7.

Here the law concerning Hebrew servants is repeated. There is an addition, requiring the masters to put some small stock into their servants' hands to set up with for themselves, when sent out of their servitude, wherein they had received no wages. We may expect family blessings, the springs of family prosperity, when we make conscience of our duty to our family relations. We are to remember that we are debtors to Divine justice, and have nothing to pay with. That we are slaves, poor, and perishing. But the Lord Jesus Christ, by becoming poor, and by shedding his blood, has made a full and free provision for the payment of our debts, the ransom of our souls, and the supply of all our wants. When the gospel is clearly preached, the acceptable year of the Lord is proclaimed; the year of release of our debts, of the deliverance of our souls, and of obtaining rest in him. And as faith in Christ and love to him prevail, they will triumph over the selfishness of the heart, and over the unkindness of the world, doing away the excuses that rise from unbelief, distrust, and covetousness.

Here is a direction what to do with the firstlings. We are not now limited as the Israelites were; we make no difference between a first calf, or lamb, and the rest. Let us then look to the gospel meaning of this law, devoting ourselves and the first of our time and strength to God; and using all our comforts and enjoyments to his praise, and under the direction of his law, as we have them all by his gift.
